subject: Human Body
title: Receptors: Lock and Key
description: One-minute skill: Receptors: Lock and Key.

hook.text: Hormones flood every tissue, but only target cells respond.

buildup.text: Each cell type has specific receptors on its surface or inside. A hormone only works if its shape matches that receptor.

discovery.text: Insulin binds to receptors on muscle and fat cells. Liver cells respond to glucagon.

twist.text: Cells can increase or decrease receptor numbers. Chronic exposure to a hormone can make cells less responsive over time.

climax.text: Hormonal signaling is precise because of receptors.

punchline.text: Wrong receptor? The hormone passes right by. Precision is everything.

quiz.question: Why do hormones only affect certain cells?
options: Hormones are directed to specific cells by the brain
Only cells with matching receptors can respond to a hormone
Hormones are transported by specialized blood vessels
